geometry_edits.rationale: Open the carved threshold toward the access side to match the program contract for an active street edge.
Increase notch depth to strengthen the public void and make the entry zone more spatially usable.
Widen the opening so the ground response becomes legible across all views.
Keep the carved void low enough to read as a public court/entry seam rather than a top-level incision.
Softly reduce the twist so the dominant mass retains continuity and better supports neighborhood-living program hierarchy.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the notch/opening to the verified access side so the public threshold reads from the frontage rather than closing it off.
Broaden the notch to create a more legible and usable public void instead of a shallow cosmetic cut.
Increase the ground-opening width so the access edge is visibly decompressed and publicly readable.
Lower the notch height to keep the opening grounded and court-like rather than a high decorative incision.
Slightly extend the dominant clipped mass so the carved void remains integrated with a clear primary volume.
Reduce twisting so the section reads more like a calm occupied mass and less like an arbitrary sculptural distortion.

rationale: The candidate is coherent across the four views and keeps a single dominant stepped mass, so it is not fragmented or view-incoherent. However, the mass reads more like a compressed terraced wedge than a neighborhood-living building with a convincing active ground threshold. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is no clearly carved public entry seam, court, or undercut that directly addresses the access edge. The central/top void is small and not yet public enough to count as a meaningful courtyard figure. The silhouette is acceptable as an early massing landform, but the section logic does not yet convincingly support the program’s semantic invariants of active edge, usable public void, and calm upper hierarchy. It also over-relies on stepped subtraction without enough void depth or ground articulation. Recommended correction: preserve the dominant stepped gesture, but deepen the carved void/open-side response toward the access edge and strengthen the courtyard/terrace relationship rather than adding more tiering.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a cultural/community-center precedent; useful for courtyard and bridge logic, but not a direct match to this candidate’s heavier stepped block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a large central void and an upper connector can support a neighborhood program if the ground edge stays open and legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Contains taller perimeter elements and a more expansive campus condition than this compact neighborhood-living brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a courtyard can create public interiority and hierarchical massing without a single monolithic block.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more open and elongated, while the candidate is compressed and more vertically tiered.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long low massing with a central void and site-responsive horizontal spread can produce an active public ground figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more sectional and porous; the candidate currently reads more as a stacked wedge with a weaker public threshold.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/ribbon-like section and connected wings can preserve a calm upper mass while keeping public circulation and open space readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the same clear void depth and layered openness at the ground edge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a central void with bridges and setbacks can create a legible mixed-use massing hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the supplied views, but the frontage response is semantically weak.
The visible open space is too shallow to read as a usable public court.
Do not over-correct into a generic box; the dominant stepped gesture is the best existing asset.
